title: The worker timed out. The team still shipped.
description: A synthetic trade-capture build with four workers, a frontier fallback, and an independent review that found two high-severity defects.
limitations: Chapters reconstruct the report's workflow order, not exact timestamps or overlapping execution.
Recorded stage durations exclude host integration and repair; they are not total project wall time.
Metered OpenRouter spend excludes subscription inference. No comparable all-in cost is available.
The original review was not rerun after repairs. The original report retains a browser-QA gap.
This historical run did not use Astra or Pi. No agents are executing during replay.

stages.title: Define the work before distributing it
stages.summary: The lead produced the architecture plan for the synthetic securitized-products workspace.
evidence: Recorded planning stage: 203.673 seconds.
The plan was reviewed before worker implementation.
stages.lesson: Use explicit ownership and acceptance boundaries before assigning work.

stages.title: Challenge the plan before code
stages.summary: Claude reviewed the proposed architecture and required changes before implementation proceeded.
evidence: Read-only architecture challenge.
$1.2314075 is subscription CLI telemetry, not billed project API spend.
stages.lesson: A separate reviewer can challenge assumptions before workers inherit them.

stages.outcome: Raw fail · behavioral pass after audit
stages.title: Separate harness failures from code behavior
stages.summary: Terra delivered the domain implementation. The raw failure involved a missing dependency link and an incremental typecheck artifact outside the allowed scope.
evidence: The exact source patch integrated without initial repair.
Later review found lifecycle and required-date omissions, repaired by Codex.
stages.lesson: Preserve the raw failure and the qualified interpretation. Neither erases later defects.

stages.outcome: Raw fail · behavioral pass after audit
stages.title: The grader rejected a variable name
stages.summary: Sonnet delivered the ticket in its owned file. A private source regex expected hasErrors; the implementation used hasBookingErrors with the same behavior.
evidence: The exact blob integrated before final review.
Post-review repairs changed pristine-error display and booked-record behavior.
stages.lesson: A contaminated source check is evidence about the grader, not proof of a behavioral failure.

stages.title: A narrow assignment paid off
stages.summary: Qwen completed the bounded desk-insights component and changed only its owned file.
evidence: Typecheck, lint, and all three private checks passed.
The exact blob integrated and remained unchanged after final review.
$0.1071646 metered through OpenRouter.
stages.lesson: This run supports small, independently verifiable worker contracts.

stages.title: Thirty minutes. No implementation.
stages.summary: Kimi read 24 files and formed a detailed plan for the broader state, composition, review, blotter, and CSS assignment. It never invoked a write tool before the limit.
evidence: The timeout remains a failure and was not rerun.
Zero changed files; $0.2648436 metered spend.
All six missing workspace files were later attributed to Codex.
stages.lesson: Planning activity is not delivery. A broad assignment needs earlier checkpoints.

stages.model: Frontier host session · exact model unreported
stages.title: The lead takes over the missing work
stages.summary: Codex implemented the six missing workspace files and integrated the other worker patches.
evidence: Integration happened in the frontier host session.
Elapsed time and comparable dollar telemetry were not instrumented.
stages.lesson: Count fallback as frontier work. A successful final product does not make the failed worker successful.

stages.title: Green checks missed two workflow defects
stages.summary: Opus found that booked trades could regress to draft and that Validate cleared the ticket, breaking the Validate → Book flow.
evidence: Two high, five medium, and four low findings were recorded.
The two high-severity findings were confirmed as correct.
The review was read-only and was not rerun after repair.
stages.lesson: Independent review added value by exposing defects after local checks were green.

stages.model: Frontier host session · exact model unreported
stages.title: Repair the defects, preserve the evidence
stages.summary: Codex repaired the lifecycle and ticket-flow defects, added regression coverage, and addressed related validation and usability findings.
evidence: Repairs were validated through the repository gate, not by rewriting the original review.
The source report accepts a synthetic local mock and retains its original browser-QA gap.
Total metered OpenRouter spend: $0.3720082. Integration and repair time are missing.
stages.lesson: The result is an accepted synthetic mock with explicit limits, not production trading software.
